I’m assuming you mean **_Cleaners_**, the **2013 Crackle original web/TV series**. If you meant a different show with the same title, tell me and I’ll switch.

## What it is
**_Cleaners_** is an **American action-comedy/drama web series** produced for **Crackle**. It has a very stylized, pulpy feel — part crime thriller, part dark comedy, with a focus on two female leads caught up in the criminal underworld.

## Basic premise
The series follows **two young women who work as “cleaners”** — people who cover up or dispose of the aftermath of crimes for powerful criminal clients. Their lives get complicated when their employer’s world starts collapsing around them, and they end up on the run while dealing with assassins, gangsters, betrayals, and shifting loyalties.

The tone is generally:
- fast-paced
- violent
- glossy/stylized
- a bit campy
- more “streaming-era genre fun” than prestige drama

## Main cast I know
The leads I remember are:

- **Emmanuelle Chriqui**
- **Emily Osment**

Other cast members associated with the show include:
- **David Arquette**
- **Gina Gershon**
- **Missi Pyle**
- **Judy Reyes**

I’m being a little cautious here because ensemble web-series casts can be easy to mix up, but those are the names most strongly tied to it in my memory.

## Format / production
- **Platform:** Crackle
- **Type:** Web series / streaming series
- **Country:** United States
- **Language:** English
- **Era:** Early 2010s streaming content, when Crackle was producing a lot of original genre programming

## Style and themes
A few recurring ideas the show plays with:
- crime and cleanup as a business
- women navigating violent power structures
- loyalty vs self-preservation
- betrayal inside criminal networks
- the absurdity of professionalized crime

It leans into a **“cool criminals in a heightened world”** vibe rather than realism.

## Reception / reputation
It wasn’t a massive mainstream hit, but it’s remembered as one of those **early Crackle originals** that tried to build a bingeable, original identity for the platform. Its appeal was mostly:
- the cast
- the snappy, genre-driven premise
- the stylish crime-world setup
